source_neutral.procedure: Assess discrete dating claims about the undated correspondence bundle, with separate assessments for individual-item bounds, pairwise writing order and a bundle-level date interval. Each claim may have one or more dating clues whose accuracy, independence and relationship to the writing date are uncertain. Candidate clues are event mentions and cross-references in the letters, postmarks and envelopes, handwriting, paper and other material features, accession and custody records, dated calendars, independent event records and the bundle's present physical arrangement. Assess each clue, identify shared origins, compare separately originating evidence and record the result for each claim as a date interval or order relation. The existence of these clues in this bundle, the association of envelopes with their accompanying letters, the status of items as sent originals rather than drafts or later copies, and the treatment of the bundle as one correspondence are open claims to be checked, not supplied facts.
source_neutral.action: 1. List claims separately for each item and each pair so that support for posting date, writing date or order is not transferred between these properties. 2. For every clue bearing on a claim, record four assessments: credibility, meaning the reliability of the clue type and the authenticity and dating reliability of the instance, including postmark legibility or the coarse resolution of handwriting comparison; access, meaning whether the clue dates writing, posting, receipt, paper manufacture, the mentioned event or filing; dependence, meaning whether it derives from another clue, such as a later pencilled date inferred from the letter's content, an accession entry copied from a vendor or family description, or an arrangement imposed by a custodian who read the letters; and relevance, meaning whether it bears on the property asserted by the claim. 3. Group clues by common origin and count each group as one line of evidence regardless of its number of clues. 4. Compare each claim across these groups and against independent event records, dated calendars and dated correspondence by the same writers held elsewhere. Before using an external record, check that it was not compiled from this bundle. 5. Record each claim as convergent, contradictory or unsupported, and express its dating result as an interval or order relation. 6. Test the physical arrangement as a claim about custody or filing rather than adopting it as the initial writing sequence.
source_neutral.observables: Convergence occurs when intervals or order relations from at least two separately originating groups overlap on the same property of a claim. Examples are an event mention supplying an earliest date, a postmark on a matched envelope supplying a latest date and a reply in another letter establishing order. Contradiction occurs when intervals from different origin groups are disjoint or order relations conflict, such as a cross-reference indicating that X precedes Y while postmarks indicate the reverse. Lack of support occurs when a claim rests on a single origin group or exclusively on clues that date a different property, such as filing order, custody date or paper manufacture being used for writing date. Observable indicators of dependence include a date added in a later hand or different medium, wording or errors shared by an annotation and an accession record, and an arrangement matching a custodian's numbering.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: When independent, credible groups of clues converge, the justified absolute chronology for an item is the overlap of their bounds, expressed as an interval rather than a point date. The justified relative chronology is the order relation they jointly support. Across the bundle, these relations yield a partial order: some items are ordered relative to one another and others remain unordered. A complete sequence is warranted only if every pair is independently supported. Contradiction lowers confidence in the affected claim and leaves it unresolved. Retain both alternatives together with candidate explanations to test: a mismatched envelope, a draft or later copy, an event anticipated or recalled rather than current, or an erroneous later annotation. Without independent support, the justified result is limited to the wider available interval, such as the bundle-level interval; this neither warrants accepting nor rejecting the single clue's date. Custody dates, event dates and physical arrangement can bound or contextualise the letters but do not, by themselves, establish writing order.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: The assessment unit is an individual dating claim, not the bundle as an undivided object. Claims have three forms: letter X was written no earlier than D1 and no later than D2; letter X was written before letter Y; and the bundle falls within a specified date interval. Clues are associated with the particular claims and properties they address. Clues sharing an origin form one evidence group, and conclusions are compared across separately originating groups. Item-level intervals, pairwise relations and the bundle-level interval remain distinct. Pairwise relations combine into a partial order without requiring every item to occupy a determined position. Envelope-letter associations, original-versus-copy status, the existence of candidate clues and the bundle's composition as one correspondence remain separate open claims.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: For contradictory or unsupported claims, seek another independent source of dating evidence, re-examine the conflicting clue's access and dependence, or compare another document or reference. For contradictions, test the retained candidate explanations involving mismatched envelopes, drafts or later copies, anticipated or recalled events, and erroneous later annotations. Keep alternative chronologies on record until independent evidence excludes one.
source_neutral.limits: Stop narrowing a claim when every remaining clue belongs to an origin group already counted or when no further independent source of dating evidence is available. Record the interval at its current width. Multiple clues do not automatically constitute independent evidence. Apparent agreement may result from an undisclosed common origin: annotations, accession entries and arrangement may derive from one earlier reader's guess, and published or external records may have been compiled from these letters. Material clues can share an error: paper stock or handwriting style may persist for years, supplying the same coarse bound across many items without corroborating a narrower bound. Clues differ in what they date: a postmark dates posting, an event mention supplies an earliest writing date and may refer to a past or expected event, and an accession record dates acquisition. Apparent convergence may also result from the assessor's shared assumptions, such as treating the bundle as one continuous exchange or its present order as original, which shape readings of ambiguous clues. Credibility concerns clue-type reliability and instance authenticity. Independence often cannot be demonstrated from the items alone and may remain a judgement. No observations have been made, and no bundle contents are supplied. Which claims will converge, conflict or remain unsupported is unknown; some items may remain datable only within the bundle-level interval.
